rationale: This is an equal-weight rank ensemble of two already-archived signals (CashAdjProfitPerAccrualBloat and CashRealizedProfitability, the latter with a wrong-signed FMB slope) rather than a new mechanism, so any gain is a portfolio-blending artifact that teaches nothing about which channel is priced, and the shared oibdp/at profitability leg means the components are not as independent as claimed.

The stated logic — isolating the accrual-created portion of operating capital rather than the NOA level — is coherent and does address a real confound with the published net-operating-assets anomaly, but a five-year sum of working-capital accruals is close to five-year NOA growth, so the discriminating power versus GrossProfitGradedByBloat may be smaller than argued.

che/act is a strictly monotone transform of the archived che/(act−che), so this is a cosmetic rescaling of CashRealizedProfitability, and the stated diagnosis is internally inconsistent because the archived version was already winsorized at 1% while this proposal drops winsorization entirely.

The level-versus-flow contrast within the cash-realization channel is a legitimate untested distinction, but Δche is contaminated by financing and investing activity (equity/debt issuance, asset sales), so a positive result would be hard to attribute to earnings validation as the hypothesis requires.

A three-year moving average of an already-tested annual signal is a smoothing variant, not a substantively different construct, and since the underlying ratio is annual the MA mostly adds stale information rather than isolating a persistent state.

Reframing the conditioner from a transient flow to a chronic accrual-policy state is a defensible response to the flow family's strong-slope/weak-alpha pattern, but the three-year mean accrual is nearly the same object as this batch's five-year accrual sum and as the archived ProfitVsAccrualBloatTrend, so the two flow-smoothing proposals are largely redundant with each other.
